objects.description: Configuration structure for the MooseFS I/O client layer. Holds master server connection parameters, mountpoint, cache sizes, logging, readahead settings, error behaviors, and minimal acceptable master version. Used with mfs_set_defaults and mfs_init to configure and initialize the library.
An ACL entry identifying a user or group by numeric id with associated permission bits. Used inside mfsacl.namedacls.

Access Control List structure for files. Contains base perms (user, group, other), optional mask, counts of named user/group ACL entries, and a flexible array of mfsaclid entries (declared as size 1 but intended for variable sizing).

functions.name: mfs_mknod
functions.signature: int mfs_mknod(const char *path, mode_t mode, dev_t dev);
functions.description: Create a filesystem node (regular file, device, or named pipe) at the given path in the MooseFS-mounted namespace. Mirrors POSIX mknod behavior.
requirements: path must point to a NUL-terminated path string within the mounted MooseFS namespace
If creating a device node, mode must specify the file type (e.g., S_IFCHR/S_IFBLK) and dev encodes the device numbers
Caller should check the integer return value for success (0) or error (-1) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_unlink
functions.description: Remove (unlink) a name from the filesystem; deletes the file when its link count reaches zero. POSIX-like semantics.
requirements: path must be a valid NUL-terminated path
Target should not be a directory; use mfs_rmdir for directories
Caller must check return value (0 on success, -1 on error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_mkdir
functions.description: Create a new directory at path with the given permissions. POSIX-like mkdir.
requirements: path must be a valid NUL-terminated path
mode specifies permission bits; umask may modify the final mode
Caller must check return value (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_rename
functions.description: Rename or move a file or directory from src to dst atomically within the filesystem. Mirrors POSIX rename.
requirements: src and dst must be valid NUL-terminated paths
Renames across different MooseFS mount points may not be allowed
Caller must check return value (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_link
functions.description: Create a new hard link at dst to the existing file at src. POSIX-like link.
requirements: src and dst must be valid paths
Target must be a regular file supported for hard-linking in MooseFS
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_symlink
functions.description: Create a symbolic link path2 that points to path1. POSIX-like symlink.
requirements: path1 is the link target string; path2 is the symlink to create
Both parameters must be valid NUL-terminated strings
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_readlink
functions.signature: ssize_t mfs_readlink(const char *path, char *buf, size_t bufsize);
functions.description: Read the contents of a symbolic link at path into buf (not NUL-terminated). Returns number of bytes placed in buf. POSIX-like readlink.
requirements: path must be a valid symlink path
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least bufsize bytes
bufsize must be greater than 0 to read any data
Caller must use return value to know actual bytes written; no NUL terminator is appended

functions.name: mfs_rmdir
functions.description: Remove an existing empty directory at path. POSIX-like rmdir.
requirements: path must be a valid directory path
Directory must be empty
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_chmod
functions.description: Change permissions of the file or directory at path to mode. POSIX-like chmod.
requirements: path must be valid
mode is a set of permission bits
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fchmod
functions.description: Change permissions of an open file referred to by descriptor fildes. POSIX-like fchmod.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open file descriptor from mfs_open
mode is a set of permission bits
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_chown
functions.signature: int mfs_chown(const char *path, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
functions.description: Change owner and group of the file at path. POSIX-like chown.
requirements: path must be valid
owner and/or group may be set to (uid_t)-1/(gid_t)-1 to leave unchanged (typical POSIX pattern)
Requires appropriate privileges
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fchown
functions.signature: int mfs_fchown(int fildes, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
functions.description: Change owner and group of an open file via descriptor. POSIX-like fchown.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor
owner/group typically may be set to (uid_t)-1/(gid_t)-1 to leave unchanged
Requires appropriate privileges
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_truncate
functions.description: Truncate or extend the file at path to exactly size bytes. POSIX-like truncate.
requirements: path must be valid
size must be non-negative
If extending, new bytes are typically zero-filled
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_ftruncate
functions.description: Truncate or extend the open file referenced by fildes to size bytes. POSIX-like ftruncate.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor with write permission when shrinking/expanding (per POSIX patterns)
size must be non-negative
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_utimes
functions.signature: int mfs_utimes(const char *path, const struct timeval times[2]);
functions.description: Set access and modification times of the file at path using timeval resolution. POSIX-like utimes.
requirements: path must be valid
times must be NULL or point to an array of two struct timeval entries [atime, mtime]
Caller must check return value (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_futimes
functions.signature: int mfs_futimes(int fildes, const struct timeval times[2]);
functions.description: Set access and modification times on an open file descriptor with timeval precision. POSIX-like futimes.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor
times must be NULL or point to two struct timeval entries [atime, mtime]
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_futimens
functions.signature: int mfs_futimens(int fildes, const struct timespec times[2]);
functions.description: Set file timestamps on an open descriptor with nanosecond precision. Supports UTIME_NOW and UTIME_OMIT as defined in the header. POSIX-like futimens.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor
times must point to an array of two struct timespec entries [atime, mtime], or be non-NULL per usage; special constants UTIME_NOW/UTIME_OMIT may be used in tv_nsec
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_lseek
functions.signature: off_t mfs_lseek(int fildes, off_t offset, int whence);
functions.description: Reposition the file offset of the open file descriptor. POSIX-like lseek.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor supporting seeking
whence should be one of SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, SEEK_END (POSIX)
Return value is new offset or -1 on error; caller must handle errno

functions.name: mfs_statvfs
functions.description: Retrieve filesystem statistics for the filesystem containing path. POSIX-like statvfs.
requirements: path must be valid
buf must point to a writable struct statvfs
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fstatvfs
functions.description: Retrieve filesystem statistics for the filesystem of the open descriptor. POSIX-like fstatvfs.
requirements: fildes must be a valid descriptor
buf must be a writable pointer to struct statvfs
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_stat
functions.description: Get file status information for path. POSIX-like stat.
requirements: path must be valid
buf must point to a writable struct stat
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fstat
functions.description: Get file status information for an open descriptor. POSIX-like fstat.
requirements: fildes must be valid
buf must point to a writable struct stat
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_open
functions.description: Open a file at path with specified flags, optionally creating it with a mode when O_CREAT is set. POSIX-like open.
requirements: path must be valid
oflag is a bitmask of open flags (e.g., O_RDONLY, O_WRONLY, O_RDWR, O_CREAT, O_TRUNC) per POSIX patterns
If O_CREAT is specified, a third argument of type mode_t must be provided
Returns a non-negative file descriptor on success or -1 on error; caller must handle errno

functions.name: mfs_read
functions.description: Read up to nbyte bytes from the open file descriptor into buf. POSIX-like read.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least nbyte bytes
nbyte may be zero; return value is number of bytes read or -1 on error

functions.name: mfs_pread
functions.description: Read from the open file descriptor at the given offset without changing the file position. POSIX-like pread.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor supporting random access
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least nbyte bytes
offset must be non-negative
Return value is bytes read or -1 on error

functions.name: mfs_write
functions.description: Write up to nbyte bytes from buf to the open file descriptor at the current file position. POSIX-like write.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor opened for writing
buf must point to at least nbyte bytes of readable memory
Return value is bytes written or -1 on error; partial writes are possible

functions.name: mfs_pwrite
functions.signature: ssize_t mfs_pwrite(int fildes,const void *buf,size_t nbyte,off_t offset);
functions.description: Write nbyte bytes from buf to the file at the specified offset without changing the file position. POSIX-like pwrite.
requirements: fildes must be valid and opened for writing
buf must be readable for at least nbyte bytes
offset must be non-negative
Return value is bytes written or -1 on error; partial writes possible

functions.name: mfs_fsync
functions.description: Synchronize file data and metadata of the open descriptor to stable storage. POSIX-like fsync.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor
Caller must check return value (0 success, -1 error)

functions.name: mfs_close
functions.description: Close an open file descriptor obtained from mfs_open. POSIX-like close.
requirements: fildes must be a valid open descriptor; do not reuse after successful close
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_flock
functions.description: Apply or remove an advisory lock on an open file descriptor. Mirrors POSIX/4.4BSD flock semantics.
requirements: fildes must be a valid descriptor
op specifies lock operation (e.g., LOCK_SH, LOCK_EX, LOCK_UN; may include LOCK_NB)
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_lockf
functions.signature: int mfs_lockf(int fildes, int function, off_t size);
functions.description: Apply or test section locks on an open file using lockf-style API layered on fcntl locks. POSIX-like lockf.
requirements: fildes must be valid
function indicates operation (e.g., F_LOCK, F_TLOCK, F_ULOCK, F_TEST per typical lockf)
size indicates number of bytes to lock relative to current offset; may be 0 to EOF (typical)
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fcntl_locks
functions.signature: int mfs_fcntl_locks(int fildes, int function, struct flock *fl);
functions.description: Perform record locking operations using fcntl-style locks via struct flock. POSIX-like fcntl locking subset.
requirements: fildes must be valid
function should be a locking-related command (e.g., F_SETLK, F_SETLKW, F_GETLK)
fl must point to a valid struct flock for the operation and may be modified by the call
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_getxattr
functions.signature: ssize_t mfs_getxattr(const char *path, const char *name, void *value, size_t size);
functions.description: Get the value of the extended attribute name for the file at path, writing up to size bytes into value. POSIX-like getxattr.
requirements: path and name must be valid NUL-terminated strings
value may be NULL to query size (return will be size needed)
If value is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least size bytes
Returns number of bytes placed in value or required size; -1 on error

functions.name: mfs_fgetxattr
functions.signature: ssize_t mfs_fgetxattr(int fildes, const char *name, void *value, size_t size);
functions.description: Get extended attribute name for an open file descriptor. POSIX-like fgetxattr.
requirements: fildes must be valid
name must be a valid attribute name
value may be NULL to obtain required size; else must have at least size bytes
Check return value (>=0 bytes, -1 error)

functions.name: mfs_setxattr
functions.signature: int mfs_setxattr(const char *path, const char *name, const void *value, size_t size, int flags);
functions.description: Set extended attribute name on path to the given value of length size. Supports flags XATTR_CREATE and XATTR_REPLACE defined in the header. POSIX-like setxattr.
requirements: path and name must be valid strings
value must point to at least size bytes of data (or may be NULL when size is 0)
flags may include XATTR_CREATE to create only, XATTR_REPLACE to replace only
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fsetxattr
functions.signature: int mfs_fsetxattr(int fildes, const char *name, const void *value, size_t size, int flags);
functions.description: Set extended attribute on an open file descriptor. POSIX-like fsetxattr.
requirements: fildes must be valid
name must be valid
value must point to at least size bytes (or NULL when size is 0)
flags use XATTR_CREATE/XATTR_REPLACE semantics
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_listxattr
functions.signature: ssize_t mfs_listxattr(const char *path, char *list, size_t size);
functions.description: List extended attribute names associated with path. Writes a concatenation of NUL-terminated names into list. POSIX-like listxattr.
requirements: path must be valid
list may be NULL to obtain required buffer size; else must have at least size bytes
Return value is number of bytes required/written; -1 on error

functions.name: mfs_flistxattr
functions.signature: ssize_t mfs_flistxattr(int fildes, char *list, size_t size);
functions.description: List extended attribute names for an open file descriptor. POSIX-like flistxattr.
requirements: fildes must be valid
list may be NULL to query size; else must provide at least size bytes
Return value is bytes written/required; -1 on error

functions.name: mfs_removexattr
functions.description: Remove the extended attribute name from the file at path. POSIX-like removexattr.
requirements: path and name must be valid strings
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fremovexattr
functions.description: Remove an extended attribute name from an open file descriptor. POSIX-like fremovexattr.
requirements: fildes must be valid
name must be a valid attribute name
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_acl_alloc
functions.description: Allocate an mfsacl structure with space for namedaclscnt named ACL entries (users and groups). Use mfs_acl_free to release. Purpose: prepare an ACL record for setfacl or local manipulation.
requirements: namedaclscnt specifies the total number of named ACL IDs to allocate space for
Caller must free the returned pointer with mfs_acl_free when no longer needed
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check for NULL before use

functions.name: mfs_acl_free
functions.description: Free an mfsacl structure previously allocated by mfs_acl_alloc or returned by mfs_getfacl/mfs_fgetfacl.
requirements: aclrec must be either NULL or a pointer obtained from mfs_acl_alloc/mfs_getfacl/mfs_fgetfacl
Do not use aclrec after freeing

functions.name: mfs_getfacl
functions.signature: int mfs_getfacl(const char *path, uint8_t acltype, mfsacl **aclrec);
functions.description: Fetch an ACL of type acltype (ACL_TYPE_ACCESS or ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT) for path and return it via aclrec. Caller is responsible for freeing the returned ACL with mfs_acl_free.
requirements: path must be valid
acltype should be ACL_TYPE_ACCESS or ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT as defined in the header
aclrec must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated mfsacl*
On success, *aclrec points to an allocated ACL that the caller must free with mfs_acl_free
Return 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fgetfacl
functions.signature: int mfs_fgetfacl(int filedes, uint8_t acltype, mfsacl **aclrec);
functions.description: Fetch an ACL of type acltype for an open file descriptor and return it via aclrec. Caller must free with mfs_acl_free.
requirements: filedes must be a valid open descriptor
acltype should be ACL_TYPE_ACCESS or ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT
aclrec must be non-NULL; on success *aclrec must be freed with mfs_acl_free
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_setfacl
functions.signature: int mfs_setfacl(const char *path, uint8_t acltype, mfsacl *aclrec);
functions.description: Set the ACL of type acltype on path using the provided mfsacl structure. Intended to apply access/default ACLs.
requirements: path must be valid
acltype should be ACL_TYPE_ACCESS or ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT
aclrec must point to a properly initialized mfsacl structure consistent with its counts (nuserscnt/ngroupscnt and namedacls length)
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_fsetfacl
functions.signature: int mfs_fsetfacl(int filedes, uint8_t acltype, mfsacl *aclrec);
functions.description: Set the ACL of type acltype on an open file descriptor using aclrec.
requirements: filedes must be a valid open descriptor
acltype should be ACL_TYPE_ACCESS or ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT
aclrec must be a valid pointer to an initialized mfsacl
Check return (0 success, -1 error) and handle errno

functions.name: mfs_set_defaults
functions.description: Initialize an mfscfg structure with default client configuration values for MooseFS I/O. Use before customizing and calling mfs_init.
requirements: mcfg must be a valid, writable pointer to an mfscfg structure
Caller must call this before mfs_init to ensure sane defaults unless filling mfscfg fully by other means

functions.name: mfs_init
functions.description: Initialize the MooseFS I/O subsystem according to the provided configuration. Staged initialization: 0 initializes everything, 1 connects to master only (pre-fork section), 2 initializes everything else (post-fork section).
requirements: mcfg must point to a valid, initialized mfscfg (e.g., via mfs_set_defaults plus customizations)
stage must be 0, 1, or 2 as documented in the header comments
If using staged init, call with stage 1 before forking, and stage 2 after forking
Return 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must handle errno

functions.name: mfs_term
functions.description: Shut down and release resources used by the MooseFS I/O subsystem. Complements mfs_init.
requirements: Should be called once when MooseFS I/O usage is complete
Do not call other mfs_* I/O functions after termination until reinitialized

data_types.description: A NUL-terminated path string referring to a file or directory within the test/mount namespace. May be absolute or relative, may or may not exist. Used wherever the API expects a pathname.
An arbitrary NUL-terminated byte string without specific format requirements. May contain any bytes except embedded NUL; used as a symlink target text for creation functions.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a single bytes buffer intended to be parsed by the fuzzing harness
# as a filename (FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME) or generic string (FUZZ_PARAM_STR) used as path-like inputs.
#
# Strategy:
# - Construct a realistic path within a virtual workspace, including combinations of:
#   - absolute or relative
#   - nested directories with varying names
#   - special names like ".", "..", hidden files, long components, unicode
#   - optional trailing slash, duplicate slashes
#   - extensions and device-like names
# - Keep result <= 4096 bytes
# - Deterministic randomness via provided seed
#
# The output is a single bytes string; the fuzzer environment maps FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to
# an on-disk temp path that contains this string content, but many harnesses accept arbitrary
# NUL-terminated C-strings for paths, so we ensure no embedded NUL and proper UTF-8 encoding.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.,@+#%="

UNICODE_COMPONENTS = [
    "żółć",
    "文件",
    "файл",
    "नाम",
    "ファイル",
    "ملف",
    "Δεδομένα",
]

SPECIAL_COMPONENTS = [
    ".",
    "..",
    ".hidden",
    "-leadingdash",
    "_underscore",
    "spaced name",
    "trailing.",
    "con",
    "nul",
    "prn",
    "aux",
    "com1",
    "lpt1",
]

EXTENSIONS = ["", ".txt", ".bin", ".dat", ".log", ".sock", ".fifo", ".dev", ".raw", ".acl"]

DEVICE_LIKE = ["tty0", "zero", "null", "random", "sda1", "loop0", "nvme0n1p1"]

def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

def rand_component(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pick = rng.randint(0, 9)
    if pick == 0:
        # unicode heavy
        base = rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_COMPONENTS)
        tail = rand_ascii(rng, 0, 6)
        return (base + tail).strip()
    elif pick == 1:
        return rand_choice(rng, SPECIAL_COMPONENTS)
    elif pick == 2:
        # long component
        return rand_ascii(rng, 50, 120)
    elif pick == 3:
        # device-like
        return rand_choice(rng, DEVICE_LIKE)
    elif pick == 4:
        # numeric-heavy
        return str(rng.randint(0, 10**9))
    elif pick == 5:
        # date-like
        return f"{rng.randint(1970,2099)}-{rng.randint(1,12):02d}-{rng.randint(1,28):02d}"
    elif pick == 6:
        # dotted segments
        return rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8) + "." + rand_ascii(rng, 2, 4)
    elif pick == 7:
        # hidden long
        return "." + rand_ascii(rng, 8, 32)
    elif pick == 8:
        return rand_ascii(rng, 1, 16)
    else:
        # mixed
        return rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8) + rng.choice(['-', '_', '.', '@']) + rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8)

def assemble_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Absolute or relative
    absolute = rng.random() < 0.5
    allow_dup_slashes = rng.random() < 0.2
    components: List[str] = []

    # Depth selection: include shallow to deep, ensuring valid and interesting
    depth = rng.randint(1, 6)

    for i in range(depth):
        comp = rand_component(rng)
        # Ensure no empty after stripping, replace with 'x'
        if comp == "":
            comp = "x"
        # Avoid NUL and slashes inside component
        comp = comp.replace("/", "-")
        components.append(comp)

    # Decide on a filename or final directory component with optional extension
    filename_like = rng.random() < 0.8
    if filename_like:
        base = components[-1]
        # Occasionally pick a specific interesting leaf name
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            base = rand_choice(rng, [
                "README",
                "a",
                "0",
                "." ,
                "..",
                "link_target",
                "symlink",
                "hardlink_src",
                "xattr.name",
                "acl.record",
            ])
        ext = rand_choice(rng, EXTENSIONS)
        leaf = (base if base not in [".", ".."] else base + "_dot") + ext
        components[-1] = leaf

    # Optionally append a trailing slash (for directories)
    trailing_slash = (not filename_like) or (rng.random() < 0.15)

    sep = "//" if allow_dup_slashes else "/"
    path = ("/" if absolute else "") + sep.join(components)
    if trailing_slash and not path.endswith("/"):
        path += "/"

    # Occasionally introduce ./ or ../ prefixes for relative paths
    if not absolute and rng.random() < 0.4:
        prefix = rand_choice(rng, ["./", "../", "././", ".././"])
        path = prefix + path

    # Bound total length and sanitize
    # Ensure not empty and no NULs
    path = path[:4000]
    if path == "":
        path = "."
    if "\x00" in path:
        path = path.replace("\x00", "") or "."

    return path

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build multiple candidate paths and pick one that exercises variety across calls
    # Some fuzzer stubs create, link, rename, use xattrs, ACLs, etc. We bias towards names
    # that are valid but diverse.
    candidates = []
    num = rng.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(num):
        p = assemble_path(rng)
        candidates.append(p)

    # Choose one candidate with weighted preferences:
    # - include dots, unicode, or device-like tokens
    def score(p: str) -> int:
        s = 0
        if any(tok in p for tok in ["/./", "/../", "//"]):
            s += 2
        if any(u in p for u in UNICODE_COMPONENTS):
            s += 2
        if any(d in p for d in DEVICE_LIKE):
            s += 1
        if p.endswith('/'):
            s += 1
        if any(ext and p.endswith(ext) for ext in EXTENSIONS if ext):
            s += 1
        if ".hidden" in p or "." in os.path.basename(p):
            s += 1
        return s

    best = max(candidates, key=score)

    # Encode as UTF-8 bytes without NUL terminator (harness treats as C-string and will add if needed)
    data = best.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Guarantee the buffer isn't empty
    if not data:
        data = b"."
    # Ensure size limit
    return data[:4096]

import os
import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator targets fuzz stubs that request:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): paths used for open/attr/symlink creation
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): generic strings for attribute names, values, symlink targets, and data payloads
# - FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int): general-purpose integers (flags, sizes, offsets)
#
# We will encode a small corpus of interesting, valid entries and pack them into a single
# bytes buffer that the harness will slice from. The goal is to provide:
# - Realistic and edge-case file paths (absolute, relative, nested, with dots, unicode)
# - Attribute names (namespaced and plain)
# - String payloads including text, binary-like, and size-varied content
# - Integers with edge-case values (0, 1, powers of two, max 32-bit, large offsets)
# The data must be valid (no embedded NULs inside strings; we will NUL-terminate each string).
# Total size kept under 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

# Helper to ensure no NUL in strings (FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects C-string without embedded NUL)
def _sanitize_no_nul(s: str) -> str:
    return s.replace('\x00', '')

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,:+@#%[](){}!$^&=~"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _rand_bytes_printable(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Allow a wide printable range, avoid NUL
    alphabet = (string.printable.replace('\x0b', '').replace('\x0c', '')).encode('utf-8')
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _pick(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def _u32_edge_values() -> List[int]:
    return [
        0, 1, 2, 3,
        7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256,
        511, 512, 1023, 1024, 2047, 2048, 4095, 4096,
        8191, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65535, 65536,
        1048575, 1048576, 1<<20, 1<<24, (1<<31)-1, (1<<31), (1<<32)-1
    ]

def _build_path_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Include absolute, relative, nested, special names, unicode; all without NULs
    base_names = [
        "file", "data", "test", "a", "b", "c", "zero", "one", "attr", "⛄", "µfile", "名字", "スペース",
        ".hidden", "..dot", "dash-file", "under_score", "mix.123", "name.with.many.dots"
    ]
    exts = ["", ".txt", ".bin", ".dat", ".log", ".conf", ".xattr"]
    dirs = [
        ".", "..", "/", "/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/mfs", "/mnt/mfs", "./sub", "subdir", "dir",
        "deep/nested/dir", "/deep/nested/dir", "./a/b/c"
    ]
    corpus = [
        "/", ".", "..",
        "/tmp/mfs_fuzz", "relative", "./relative", "../up", "./.hidden",
    ]
    # Compose random paths
    for _ in range(30):
        d = _pick(rng, dirs)
        n = _pick(rng, base_names) + _pick(rng, exts)
        if d.endswith('/') or d in ("/",):
            p = d + n if d != "/" else "/" + n
        elif d in (".", ".."):
            p = d + "/" + n
        else:
            p = d + "/" + n
        # Occasionally add deeper component
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            p += "/" + _pick(rng, base_names)
        corpus.append(p)
    # Add a few long-ish paths
    long_components = ["long" + "a"*rng.randint(10, 40) for _ in range(3)]
    corpus.append("/" + "/".join(long_components))
    return list(dict.fromkeys(_sanitize_no_nul(p) for p in corpus))

def _build_attr_name_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Common xattr namespaces and names; plus random names
    names = [
        "user.comment", "user.desc", "user.checksum", "user.meta", "user.key",
        "system.posix_acl_access", "system.posix_acl_default",
        "trusted.mfs", "security.selinux", "user.😀", "user.名字", "user.a", "user.b",
    ]
    for _ in range(20):
        names.append("user." + _sanitize_no_nul(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 16)))
    return list(dict.fromkeys(names))

def _build_payload_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    payloads: List[bytes] = []
    # Small, typical strings
    small_texts = [
        b"hello", b"world", b"data", b"payload", b"value", b"attr", b"symlink-target",
        b"quick brown fox", b"lorem ipsum", b"mfs fuzz"
    ]
    payloads.extend(small_texts)
    # Random printable of varied sizes
    for size in [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 768, 1023]:
        if size == 0:
            payloads.append(b"")
        else:
            payloads.append(_rand_bytes_printable(rng, size, size))
    # Some patterned bytes
    payloads.append(bytes([i % 256 for i in range(100)]))
    payloads.append(b"A" * 100)
    payloads.append(b"\x01\x02\x03\x04" * 50)
    return payloads

def _build_symlink_targets(paths: List[str], rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # symlink target can be any string; use mix of absolute, relative, and arbitrary text
    targets = [
        "/does/not/exist", "../relative/target", "./same/dir", "/tmp/target", "target", "linkdest",
        "..", ".", "/", "../../up", "a/b/c", "nested/target",
    ]
    # include some valid paths from our path corpus
    targets.extend(paths[:10])
    # add random ascii strings
    for _ in range(10):
        targets.append(_sanitize_no_nul(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 24)))
    return list(dict.fromkeys(targets))

def _pack_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Pack as: u32 count, then for each: u32 len (including NUL), bytes + NUL
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack('<I', len(strings))
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8')
        # ensure no embedded NUL; add terminator
        b = b.replace(b'\x00', b'')
        out += struct.pack('<I', len(b) + 1)
        out += b + b'\x00'
    return bytes(out)

def _pack_blobs(blobs: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Similar to strings but raw bytes, with length prefix (no enforced NUL)
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack('<I', len(blobs))
    for b in blobs:
        out += struct.pack('<I', len(b))
        out += b
    return bytes(out)

def _pack_u32_list(values: List[int]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack('<I', len(values))
    for v in values:
        out += struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build corpora
    paths = _build_path_corpus(rng)
    attr_names = _build_attr_name_corpus(rng)
    payloads = _build_payload_corpus(rng)
    symlink_targets = _build_symlink_targets(paths, rng)

    # Build integers: sizes (0..1024), offsets, flags choices
    u32_values = []
    # Edge values
    u32_values.extend(_u32_edge_values())
    # Sizes primarily within 0..1024 for the fuzz stub usage
    for _ in range(32):
        u32_values.append(rng.randrange(0, 1025))
    # Offsets including larger values
    for _ in range(16):
        shift = rng.choice([0, 10, 16, 20, 24, 28])
        base = rng.randrange(0, 1 << (32 - shift))
        u32_values.append((base << shift) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    # Flags-like small integers
    u32_values.extend([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])
    # Deduplicate while keeping order
    seen = set()
    u32_values = [x for x in u32_values if (x not in seen and not seen.add(x))]

    # Shuffle slices to vary per seed
    rng.shuffle(paths)
    rng.shuffle(attr_names)
    rng.shuffle(symlink_targets)
    rng.shuffle(payloads)
    rng.shuffle(u32_values)

    # Trim corpora to keep total size under limit
    # Heuristic budgets
    max_paths = 40
    max_names = 40
    max_targets = 30
    max_payloads = 30
    max_u32 = 128

    paths = paths[:max_paths]
    attr_names = attr_names[:max_names]
    symlink_targets = symlink_targets[:max_targets]
    payloads = payloads[:max_payloads]
    u32_values = u32_values[:max_u32]

    # Assemble final buffer with a simple header to help the harness parse sequentially:
    # Layout:
    #  magic "MFSF" (4)
    #  section 1: filenames (strings)
    #  section 2: generic strings (for names/values/targets combined)
    #  section 3: payload blobs
    #  section 4: u32 values
    # For section 2 we will include both attr names and symlink targets and a few random extras

    generic_strings: List[str] = []
    generic_strings.extend(attr_names)
    generic_strings.extend(symlink_targets)
    # Add some additional generic strings for payload-as-string (used by setxattr value path)
    for _ in range(10):
        generic_strings.append(_sanitize_no_nul(_rand_ascii(rng, 0, 40)))
    # Include some of the filenames also as possible strings
    generic_strings.extend(paths[:10])

    # Deduplicate generics preserving order
    seen = set()
    tmp = []
    for s in generic_strings:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            tmp.append(s)
    generic_strings = tmp

    # Now pack sections
    parts = []
    parts.append(b"MFSF")
    parts.append(_pack_strings(paths))
    parts.append(_pack_strings(generic_strings))
    parts.append(_pack_blobs(payloads))
    parts.append(_pack_u32_list(u32_values))

    buf = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure size constraint
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        # If too large, reduce lists further and repack
        cut_ratio = MAX_TOTAL_SIZE / len(buf)
        def cut(lst, ratio):
            n = max(1, int(len(lst) * ratio))
            return lst[:n]
        paths_cut = cut(paths, cut_ratio)
        generics_cut = cut(generic_strings, cut_ratio)
        payloads_cut = cut(payloads, cut_ratio)
        u32_cut = cut(u32_values, cut_ratio)
        parts = []
        parts.append(b"MFSF")
        parts.append(_pack_strings(paths_cut))
        parts.append(_pack_strings(generics_cut))
        parts.append(_pack_blobs(payloads_cut))
        parts.append(_pack_u32_list(u32_cut))
        buf = b"".join(parts)

    return buf
